data.name: Dola
data.gender_notes: Dola is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Dola is the name of a divine female figure, often depicted as a spinner or dancer. She is also associated with the goddess Durga and represents the cyclical nature of time and the universe. The name Dola carries the meaning “Spinner, Dancer” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dola usually hope their child will grow to embody spinner, dancer and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of the continuous cycle of life and creation.
data.etymology: Dola belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Spinner, Dancer.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dola total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Dola is most famously associated with the traditional Bengali festival of Dola Purnima, also known as Shankh Chainti or Dol Jatra. During this festival, married women visit Shashti temples dressed as Dola, the divine princess. They carry a decorative swing, called a dolchhador, and Circle around the temple, symbolizing a return to the divine source and the union of Shiva and Shakti.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Dola signifies the cyclical nature of time and the universe. In Hinduism, Dola represents the divine feminine energy or Shakti, and her dance symbolizes the ongoing cycle of creation, destruction, and regeneration. She is also a symbol of marital bliss and devotion, as seen in the Dola Purnima festival where women seek the blessings of the Divine Couple, Shiva and Shakti, and strengthen their own marital bonds.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dola signifies the eternal, rhythmic cycle of life and the divine play of Lord Krishna with his consort Radha. It embodies the joy, love, and grace of these divine dances, symbolizing harmony, balance, and the continuous flow of life's energies.
